rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should test a balanced multimodal setup with strong components (pca_n2000 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, weighted fusion) to establish a baseline for performance. This configuration isolates the effect of multimodal integration and fusion strategies, which are critical design choices. It is the best use of the first experiment to learn about the potential value of combining RNA and image data.

The existing evidence only includes config_002 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted fusion). This experiment tests whether using only RNA data (config_001) achieves comparable performance, isolating the effect of multimodal fusion. It directly compares single vs multimodal approaches with identical RNA encoder and aggregation settings, addressing the critical question of whether image data contributes meaningfully. This is the best use of the next experiment as it reduces uncertainty about the value of multimodal inputs while keeping other design choices constant.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models (config_002) outperform RNA-only (config_001) with validation accuracy 0.635 vs 0.591. This experiment tests the impact of fusion method (concat vs weighted) while keeping RNA/image encoders and aggregation the same. It isolates the effect of fusion strategy, a critical design choice, to determine if the current weighted fusion in config_002 is optimal. This balances exploitation of the promising multimodal direction with exploration of key architectural decisions.

Existing evidence shows multimodal models (config_002) outperform RNA-only (config_001) with weighted fusion. This experiment tests transformer aggregation (vs avgpool in config_002) while keeping fusion method consistent (weighted), isolating the effect of aggregation. It addresses uncertainty about whether transformer aggregation improves performance, a critical design choice with potential for significant gains.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with weighted fusion and pca_n2000 RNA encoder (config_002) achieve the highest accuracy. This experiment tests the effect of switching the RNA encoder to scvi_n200 while using transformer aggregation and concat fusion, isolating the impact of representation and aggregation methods. It balances exploration of RNA encoder variants with minimal changes to other parameters, providing insight into whether scvi_n200 could improve performance without altering the image encoder or fusion strategy.

Existing evidence shows that config_003 (scvi_n200 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) achieves the highest accuracy (0.7207). This experiment tests the effect of changing fusion type from concat to weighted while keeping other parameters identical, isolating the impact of fusion strategy. It balances exploitation (building on the successful scvi_n200 + transformer combination) and exploration (testing a critical design choice with potential to improve performance).

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (as in config_035) achieves high performance. This experiment tests whether switching the image encoder from imagenet_vit_l to resnet50 (while keeping other parameters the same) improves accuracy. This isolates the impact of the image encoder choice, a critical design decision with uncertain optimal value.

Existing evidence shows that models with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_035) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests the impact of using concat fusion instead of weighted fusion with the same transformer aggregation, while varying RNA encoder (scgpt) and image encoder (resnet50). It isolates the effect of fusion method and encoder choices, which are critical design decisions, without altering other high-performing components like multiprofile setup and transformer aggregation.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion achieve high accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests whether using singleprofile instead of multiprofile (while keeping RNA encoder and image encoder the same) improves performance, isolating the impact of profile setting. It also compares aggregation methods (transformer vs None) to understand their relative importance.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and weighted fusion with transformer aggregation achieves high accuracy (0.7249). This experiment tests replacing transformer aggregation with avgpool while keeping other parameters the same, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It clarifies whether transformer's superiority is robust or if avgpool could offer comparable performance, balancing exploitation of current trends with exploration of critical design choices.
